question: How does annealing temperature affect crystallinity and creep deformation behavior of β-nucleated isotactic polypropylene under varying environmental conditions?
answer: Annealing temperature promotes the second crystallization of β-nucleated isotactic polypropylene, leading to increased crystallinity. At low environmental temperatures and small tensile stresses, annealed samples exhibit accelerated creep deformation due to reduced coupling force in the crystalline hard skeleton, despite higher crystallinity. At high environmental temperatures and large tensile stresses, creep deformation is mainly determined by crystallinity, with higher crystallinity correlating to greater creep resistance. Additionally, crystalline morphology influences creep resistance, with bundlelike spherulites providing higher resistance than radial spherulites under all conditions.
